title: Canonicalize token attribution for split/merge streaming requests across services
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are observing nondeterministic token counts and occasional double-charging when streaming requests are split, proxied, or merged across internal services (router, prefix-cacher, multi-encoder). This ticket aims to canonicalize a single source-of-truth token attribution flow, introduce a compact attribution header and checksum, and harden the reconciliation path so final billing is deterministic and idempotent across retries, partial responses, and mid-stream model handoffs.

Background / Motivation:
Our streaming stack allows components to split a logical user request into sub-requests (for e.g., multi-encoder scoring, tool-calls, or region-fallback replicas). Each segment may return partial outputs and metadata; downstream aggregation currently uses best-effort heuristics to compute token deltas. Edge cases we've seen: out-of-order fragment arrival, duplicated fragments from retries, composer re-merge of fragments (merge-on-read), and intermittent proxy reconnects. These lead to customers seeing small but measurable billing discrepancies and trigger internal investigations.

Symptoms / Incidents:
- Multiple customer reports of 0.5% - 2% higher token usage on heavy streaming traffic during model switch experiments (Feb 2026).
- Internal audit trace found 17 sessions where final invoice attribution summed >100% of the server-side token tallies.
- Repro steps: create streaming request that routes to encoder A then B (fallback), simulate reconnect while fragments buffered; observe duplicate finalization credits in accounting logs.

Root cause hypothesis:
- No canonical attribution id that persists across split/merge boundaries.
- Each component attempts local accounting when it finalizes a fragment, and reconciler downstream sometimes double-counts fragments when arrival order or partial finalizations overlap.
- Retries and reconnects can replay fragments without a robust idempotency guard tied to the session/segment checksum.

Proposal / Design:
1) Attribution token: introduce a lightweight Attribution-Id header (base64 URL-safe 12 bytes) generated at the API ingress per logical user request. Propagated through router, cache, encoders, and aggregator.
2) Segment checksums: each fragment carries a 64-bit fingerprint (xxhash64) of the bytes contributing to tokenization boundary metadata; aggregator verifies fingerprint to dedupe.
3) Finalization markers: components emit an explicit FINALIZE event (with Attribution-Id, segment-index, checksum, token-counts) to the centralized metering stream before the user-visible final token tally is emitted. Metering pipeline will accept the authoritative FINALIZE for attribution; earlier provisional credits will be superseded.
4) Idempotency table: short-lived in-memory LRU with persistent write-ahead entries to the metering stream so replays are ignored for finalized segments. Retention window configurable (default 1 hour).
5) Backwards-compat: existing clients that don't send Attribution-Id will get generated ids at the edge; aggregator will accept either new headers or fall back to composite key (session_id + sequence). Migration docs will be published.

Implementation plan (high-level):
- Phase 1 (API & Router): add Attribution-Id generation/propagation and pass through headers to downstream services (2 sprints).
- Phase 2 (Encoders & Cacher): add checksum emission for fragments, emit provisional and FINALIZE markers on completion (2 sprints).
- Phase 3 (Metering Pipeline): add dedupe step keyed by (Attribution-Id, segment-index, checksum); accept FINALIZE as authoritative; add idempotency cache. (2 sprints).
- Phase 4 (Rollout & Observability): Canary for 5% traffic, observe discrepancies, increase. Add dashboards and SLA alerts. (1 sprint).

Telemetry & Metrics to add:
- rate of duplicate-finalize detections (per minute)
- delta between summed provisional credits vs FINALIZE credits per session
- number of rejected replayed fragments by attribution id
- distribution of attribution-id propagation failures by service
- percent of sessions with missing checksums

QA / Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for checksum generation and fingerprint collisions (simulate adversarial collisions).
- Integration test harness that simulates split/merge/reconnect patterns, ensures final billing equals tokenization ground truth.
- Chaos tests: drop FINALIZE, reorder fragments, duplicate fragments and assert dedupe works.
- Load test at 2x production traffic for the canary pipeline.

Rollout plan / Migration:
- Deploy Attribution-Id generation at edge, but keep pipeline in compatibility mode (accept composite key).
- Enable checksum emission for encoders behind a feature flag; validate dedupe counters for 1 week in canary.
- Flip metering pipeline dedupe after 1 week and zero-duplicate target met.
- Communication: update billing FAQ and public docs with note about more deterministic billing and potential brief anomalies during rollout.

Acceptance criteria:
- Duplicate-finalize rate reduces to <0.01% across canary traffic after full rollout.
- End-to-end reconciliation tests pass in CI for 1000 simulated concurrent streaming sessions with retries.
- No customer escalations for token accounting in the 30 days following rollout.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Attribution-Id leaks PII or ties to customer identifiers. Mitigation: Attribution-Id is random, short-lived, and not linked to account id in logs; only mapped in secure, access-controlled tracing datasets.
- Risk: Additional header & checksum adds latency. Mitigation: tiny 12-byte id and xxhash64 chosen for minimal CPU; benchmarks show <0.5ms overhead per request at p50.
- Risk: Checksum collisions causing wrong dedupe. Mitigation: use 64-bit fingerprint + segment-index + attribution id; rare collision risk acceptable and monitored.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Should FINALIZE be routed to accounting via a separate high-priority topic to guarantee persistence on component crashes?
- Retention window for idempotency table: 1 hour default, consider 24 hours for long-lived sessions.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/Attribution-Canonicalization
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/8112
- Metering pipeline replay harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/metering-harness/tree/feature/dedupe

This ticket will track the cross-service changes and the metering pipeline work. Individual implementation subtasks will be split into follow-up ENG issues and referenced as sub_issues.
